about.title: Marysville Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Marysville's collision data tells a story local drivers already sense: crashes cluster along 10th Street, E Street, 5th Street, and B Street, with Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. seeing the heaviest reports. In a recent year, Yuba County recorded 43 injury collisions in the city, hurting 66 people and claiming 3 lives. Behind each number is someone dealing with medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster calling before the dust settles. LawProactive exists to connect injured Marysville residents with an independent personal injury attorney, free of charge, so you're not sorting through claim forms and settlement offers alone. We don't practice law or promise results — we simply make the introduction so someone with legal experience can evaluate what happened to you, protect your evidence, and speak with insurers on your behalf while you concentrate on recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or public bus — was involved. An attorney can spot that distinction early so you don't lose your right to recover.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the crash — your share of fault simply reduces the payout rather than eliminating it. That's a nuanced calculation insurers won't necessarily explain to you.

items.title: No Cap on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no limit on non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in a car accident case. An experienced attorney knows how to document and present those losses so they're taken seriously, not brushed aside.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used later to minimize your claim, even if you're simply being honest. An independent attorney can handle that communication for you.

items.question: Why do so many crashes seem to happen on Fridays in Marysville?
items.answer: Public crash records show Marysville collisions tend to peak on Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m., likely tied to end-of-week commute and school traffic converging on corridors like 10th Street and 5th Street. This is a pattern in the data, not a judgment about any particular road. If you were hurt during this window, the timing itself can sometimes help corroborate your account of events.

items.question: What if the crash happened on a city-maintained road in Marysville?
items.answer: Claims involving a government entity, such as a city-maintained street or a public vehicle, often carry a much shorter filing deadline — sometimes just six months instead of California's usual two years. Because these claims involve extra notice requirements, it's worth having an attorney review the details quickly. LawProactive can help connect you with someone who handles this type of claim.
